source_review.boundaries: Begins after XLIV on printed84; includes its following body line and the sole first body word on printed85, ending before XLV. Superscript33,34,35,1 are apparatus reference numbers, not body. Editorial star after wa is retained as documentary sign, not a pronounced letter.
source_review.fidel_and_order_comparison: The stage1 tentative kalate/mebarq spellings and expanded final meslehumu were my preliminary reading mistakes, not proposed emendations. In the reopened line, ካልእት and መብረቅ match the actual glyphs; the final crop consists of four fidels ም-ስ-ሎ-ሙ, not five including an independent h. The o-order l and final mu form the possessive noun spelling. The penultimate body is ኀ-ዲ-ገ; do not replace it with the differently ordered normal form noted in apparatus35. Connective is እፎ, not a different expected causal connector. The rising form ends ሙ; subsequent ይከውን and ይክል do not carry plural u. These final readings were confirmed after candidate exposure and are not represented as independently blind exact transcription.
source_review.critical_limits: The selected number change and compressed reference remain interpretive uncertainties. None is resolved by replacing source spelling or claiming a newly inspected manuscript.

english_review.full_text: And I saw something else concerning lightning:[a] how they arise from the stars, and it becomes lightning and cannot leave their form.[b]
english_review.assessment: The seeing report and concerning-lightning phrase are accounted for; something else is a bounded indefinite rendering of the starred other-form, not a new class or specified count. Efo gives how. Qwm permits arise/stand up; arise is legitimate here but not a unique asserted physical mechanism. Em gives from; stars is supplied by the explicit kawakebt noun, not made the explicit rising subject. The English they, then it, retains the source number change. Becomes lightning reflects singular kwana with lightning predicate. Cannot plus leave-infinitive plus their form is an object construction, not cannot remain with them. Their is deliberately unassigned beyond the printed plural possessive suffix. The result is difficult English because the selected relation is difficult, and explanation b says so.

explanations_review.assessment: Reviewed all sentences. The selected star is real and retained; the note correctly avoids turning something else into an inserted new lightning-kind or list of stars. One chapter/unit across a page break is verified from both pages.

Reviewed all sentences. Plural rising versus singular become/cannot is visually supported and not normalized. The noun their form is distinct from the suffixed with-preposition in the actual Latin173-175 entries and grammar suffix controls. No explicit rising subject or unprinted antecedent is assigned. The selected how and leave-infinitive are supported; p453 explicitly demonstrates ability + accusative infinitive + object, including cannot leave his father. Retaining the body infinitive rather than apparatus-normalizing it is correct. The note accurately warns of compressed, uncertain reference instead of asserting a fully solved meaning.

decisive_controls.finding: Actual qwm entry and continuations permit stand, arise, remain, be established; English arise is defensible, not unique.
Actual brq noun/verb entry supports lightning/flashing, without angelological additions.
Actual hdag range leave/relinquish and the ability-infinitive/object construction support cannot leave their form.
Actual kaala entry and continuations support ability; this is not a leave verb by itself.
Other/another range does not authorize a specific number or new class of lightning.
Actual kwana range includes become; actual kokab/kawakebt entry supports stars.

Noun form/similitude and preposition with have distinct suffix constructions; actual source o-order l supports their form. My stage1 h-retention shorthand was wrong for this four-fidel source and is explicitly withdrawn, not repeated as evidence.
Actual efo control supports how; alphabet and plural-u controls inform reading without supplying new witness evidence.
